name: Nate Smith
notes: The lane's drum-idiom specialist, and the entry says "the drum idiom is the whole entry". `confidence` is **low** — his standing as a groove-vocabulary source is documented, but the research marks the specific ghost-note and linear description as idiom inference from the records. Two of the five stated points are directly authorable and they are what this model is: "(1) Extremely dense **ghost-note** activity — the 16th and 32nd grid is continuously filled at very low velocity, so the audible backbeat floats on a bed of near-silent strokes; this is the single most copied modern soul drum parameter" is a ghost probability of **0.86**, the highest in the roster, at the lowest ghost velocity band here; and "(2) Hats played with a wide, non-quantised swing while the kick and snare stay near the grid" is a `swing.amount` of 0.7 against a jitter map that gives the closed hat 14 ms and the kick and snare 3 and 4 — the exact inverse of Kaytranada's arrangement of the same two layers. "Composed, repeating drum ostinati that behave like riffs rather than like time-keeping" and "no fills in the conventional sense" set `fills` at 2 and 8 bars. "As a bandleader he writes over static m9 vamps so the drum part carries the information; the harmonic bed is deliberately simple" — `maxChords` 2, a vamp harmonic rhythm, a low melodic density and a high chord-tone bias, all deliberately plain so the kit is the subject. He "pairs with a played electric bass and locks kick-to-bass rather than kick-to-click; no 808". ⚠ Every drum number, `swing.amount` and every melody figure here is INFERRED. ⚠ The linear phrasing (no two limbs striking together) and the implied half-time/double-time switches are not expressible in this schema and are not encoded. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` gained `syncopated_cell` (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry says "n/a as a harmonist", and "he writes over static m9 vamps so the drum part carries the information; the harmonic bed is deliberately simple". `chordDurationBeats` is the only parameter carrying a loop length, and it was **dead here**: `generators::chords::layout` reads it under `syncopated_cell` alone, which this model did not author — so every generation was one 4-bar hold instead of the documented loop. The sonority itself does not move: over a single-chord family every cell is the same chord re-voiced. ⚠ The cell range [8, 16] was already authored here; "vamps" plural is a bed that re-articulates, not one block chord across the clip. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 959/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.2 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "as a bandleader he writes over static m9 vamps so the drum part carries the information; the harmonic bed is deliberately simple.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
